from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Consider two blocks sliding toward a wall.", "Small block m hits large block M.", "Collisions produce digits of Pi. Amazing!"]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: An Unexpected Discovery", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare objects
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#4169E1", fill_opacity=0.6)
        label_c = Text("C", color=WHITE).next_to(circle, ORIGIN)
        c_group = VGroup(circle, label_c)
        
        square = Square(side_length=1.7, color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0.6)
        label_s = Text("S", color=WHITE).next_to(square, ORIGIN)
        s_group = VGroup(square, label_s)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(c_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(c_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#4169E1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(c_group.animate.scale(1.1), run_time=0.2)
            self.play(c_group.animate.scale(1/1.1), run_time=0.2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#4169E1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Transform(c_group, s_group))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Map velocity states onto a circle.", "Each collision rotates the velocity vector.", "Total rotation matches Pi's geometry.", "Collision count relates to arc length.", "Geometric mapping explains this Pi connection."]
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Mapping: The Circle Connection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        plane = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        point = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        point.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(0))
        projection = DashedLine(point.get_center(), [point.get_center()[0], 0, 0], color="#A9A9A9")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(plane), Create(circle))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.play(Rotate(point, angle=PI/4, about_point=circle.get_center(), run_time=2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#A9A9A9")
        self.add(projection)
        self.play(FadeIn(projection))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Rotate(point, angle=PI/4, about_point=circle.get_center(), run_time=2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Rotate(point, angle=PI/4, about_point=circle.get_center(), run_time=2))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scaling Powers of 100", [
            "Increase mass ratio by powers of 100.",
            "Observe collision counts matching Pi digits.",
            "Mass ratio 100 yields 3 collisions.",
            "10,000 ratio yields 31 collisions.",
            "1,000,000 ratio yields 314 collisions."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Increase mass ratio by powers of 100.
        expr = MathTex("100^n", font_size=48, color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_in_area(expr, "B2", "C5")
        self.play(Write(expr))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Observe collision counts matching Pi digits.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFE0")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Mass ratio 100 yields 3 collisions.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFB6C1")
        self.play(expr.animate.scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # 10,000 ratio yields 31 collisions.
        new_expr = MathTex("10000", font_size=60, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_in_area(new_expr, "B2", "C5")
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(expr, new_expr))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # 1,000,000 ratio yields 314 collisions.
        final_expr = MathTex("1000000", font_size=72, color="#98FB98")
        self.place_in_area(final_expr, "B2", "C5")
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#98FB98")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(new_expr, final_expr))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Intuition", [
            "Phase space rotations yield discrete counts.",
            "Pi emerges from conservation laws.",
            "Geometry and physics are deeply linked."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in a summary node labeled 'Main Concept'. Color: #FFFFFF.
        summary_node = Text("Main Concept", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(summary_node, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_node))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Connect the summary node to three branching sub-points. Color: #00FFFF.
        sub1 = Text("Phase Space", color="#00FFFF", font_size=20)
        sub2 = Text("Conservation", color="#00FFFF", font_size=20)
        sub3 = Text("Geometry", color="#00FFFF", font_size=20)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sub1, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(sub2, 'D4', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(sub3, 'D6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        lines = VGroup(
            Line(summary_node.get_bottom(), sub1.get_top()),
            Line(summary_node.get_bottom(), sub2.get_top()),
            Line(summary_node.get_bottom(), sub3.get_top())
        )
        
        self.play(Create(lines), FadeIn(sub1), FadeIn(sub2), FadeIn(sub3))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash all elements once to signal completion.
        self.play(Flash(summary_node), Flash(sub1), Flash(sub2), Flash(sub3))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digit Emergence
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic understanding of Newtonian mechanics

sections.title: The Hook: An Unexpected Discovery
sections.content: Introduce the counter-intuitive puzzle: How can a series of simple block collisions compute the digits of Pi? Present a visual of two blocks sliding on a frictionless surface towards a wall.
sections.example: A small block (mass m) and a large block (mass M=100m) sliding on a frictionless floor.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly review Conservation of Momentum and Conservation of Kinetic Energy. Explain that elastic collisions between blocks follow these two laws, leading to a system of equations that define the velocity updates.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'phase space' plot where the velocity of block A is the x-axis and block B is the y-axis, forming a circular arc path.

sections.title: Geometric Mapping: The Circle Connection
sections.content: Explain that the velocity states of the two blocks can be mapped onto a circle. As collisions occur, the velocity vector rotates by a specific angle. The total number of collisions corresponds to the arc length covered, mapping to Pi.
sections.example: An animation showing the velocity vector rotating around a circle every time a collision occurs; the total rotation angle is proportional to the square root of the mass ratio.

sections.title: Scaling Powers of 100
sections.content: Demonstrate that as the mass ratio M/m increases by factors of 100 (100, 10,000, 1,000,000), the number of collisions matches the digits of Pi (3, 31, 314, etc.).
sections.example: A digital counter display next to the colliding blocks showing the digits '3.14...' ticking up as the mass of the larger block increases.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Synthesize why this works: The problem is a discrete manifestation of a continuous rotation in phase space. Conclude that Pi appears whenever we look at the 'geometry' of conservation laws.
sections.example: A final visual summary: 1. Set up blocks, 2. Count collisions, 3. Reveal Pi.
